sentences.en: Today, we're tackling a very frequently requested topic and also one of the major concepts in psychology and how we conceptualize the self.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讨论一个经常被要求的话题，它也是心理学中的一个主要概念，即我们如何概念化自我。

sentences.en: So I'm actually quite surprised that I've never done a full episode on this before.
sentences.zh: 我很惊讶我以前竟然从未就此做过一期完整的节目。

sentences.en: What I'm talking about is ego, that nasty feeling we all get sometimes that maybe we're a little bit better than others, that maybe we deserve more, that life is unfair to us,
sentences.zh: 我所说的就是“自我”（ego），那种我们有时都会有的讨厌感觉：也许我们比别人好一点，也许我们理应得到更多，生活对我们不公平，

sentences.en: or we are somewhat too good for our reality.

sentences.en: That feeling is a really hard one to come to terms with.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉真的很难面对。

sentences.en: None of us like feeling entitled, and I think we can often involuntarily ignore when those feelings come up because it's shameful to admit.
sentences.zh: 我们都不喜欢感到自己有特权，我认为当这些感觉出现时，我们往往会不由自主地忽视它们，因为承认这一点很羞耻。

sentences.en: But I also think that it is still very much part of the human experience, as we're going to examine in this episode.

sentences.en: There is such a long list of explanations
sentences.zh: 关于为什么我们的自我有时会膨胀，为什么我们会这样恐惧，它在保护我们免受什么伤害，或者它实际上是如何反映了

sentences.en: surrounding why our ego is sometimes inflated, why we fear this way, what it's protecting us from, perhaps how it's actually really reflecting

sentences.en: some of our more deeply rooted insecurities.
sentences.zh: 个人而言，我最近一直在思考“自我”这个问题，思考我的现实和自我认知是基于事实，还是基于某种对自己看法上的错误观念。

sentences.en: Personally, I've been contemplating ego quite a bit recently, whether my reality and my self-perception is based on truth or some kind of false idea of how I see myself.

sentences.en: I think I'd get cut down pretty quickly, but it's much more around, am I actually worth the credit that I give myself or am I delusional?
sentences.zh: 还有，我的自信和自尊真的是自信吗？还是表现得像傲慢？

sentences.en: So we're going to discuss that today by kind of going back to some of our very rudimentary psychology and examining the very Freudian idea around ego and some of ego's friends
sentences.zh: 比如“本我”（id）和“超我”（super ego）。

sentences.en: like the id and the super ego.

sentences.zh: 以及这种特质在某些文化中比其他文化更受重视（这非常有趣），以及它对我们有什么影响。

sentences.en: and how that quality is valued in some cultures more than others, very interestingly, but also what impact that has on us.

sentences.en: And some of the crucial signs, six in particular, that it might actually be your ego in control.
sentences.zh: 我也认为，正如我之前反思和谈论的那样，自负和自信可能非常、非常相似，感觉也很像，

sentences.en: I also think, like I reflected and was talking about before, being egotistical and being confident can be very, very similar and feel very similar,
sentences.zh: 但它们绝对是截然不同的东西。

sentences.en: but they're definitely very different things.

sentences.en: Whilst I think confidence is very stable, it is this self-assurance that we know who we are, we know what we're about and how we choose to treat the people around us.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还将看看如何区分两者，以及如何从基于“自我”的行为转变为基于自尊、

sentences.en: So we're also going to look at how we can tell the difference and how to shift from acting from a place of ego to acting from a place of self-esteem,

sentences.en: humility and grace.

sentences.en: So I'm also going to give you four key tips around that, one of which is a little bit counterintuitive, but I promise you it makes sense when I explain it.
sentences.zh: 所以我迫不及待地想今天和你们讨论这一切：关于“自我”的禁忌，它对我们每个人的控制，以及我们如何接受它是人类现实的一部分，

sentences.en: So I can't wait to discuss this all with you today, the taboo of ego, the control it has over every single one of us, but also how do we accept it as part of human reality
sentences.zh: 并真正将那些冲动转化为自信。

sentences.en: and really transform those urges to ones of self-confidence.
sentences.zh: 所以我想事不宜迟，让我们讨论一下我们“自我”背后的真实心理学。

sentences.en: So I think without further ado, let's discuss the real psychology behind our egos.
sentences.zh: 如果不先了解“自我”的角色和影响，我们就无法理解我们自己，也无法理解我们更深层的自我。

sentences.en: We cannot understand ourselves and also our deeper self without first understanding the role and the influence of our ego.
sentences.zh: 它是我们是谁的重要组成部分，而且我认为，了解它是如何迫使我们以某种方式行事并对待他人的，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: It's a vital part of who we are and really, I think it's important to understand how it compels us to behave in certain ways and treat others as well.
sentences.zh: 而这种理解的核心在于审视并很好地掌握“自我”的实际起源和基础，因为看待它的方式有几种不同。

sentences.en: And innate to that understanding is examining and having a good grasp of the actual origins and the basics of ego because there's a few different ways of viewing it.

sentences.en: Some of them are helpful.

sentences.en: And I think with most psychological concepts that have been kind of extrapolated for everyday use, there is always going to be some diffusion of accuracy in how we use these terms
sentences.zh: 以及在日常生活中使用“自我”这个词并提及它时，准确性总是会存在一些偏差。

sentences.en: and how we use the term ego and refer to it throughout our daily lives.
sentences.zh: 所以首先，让我们区分通俗心理学中对“自我”的理解，与一些更深层的

sentences.en: So firstly, let's distinguish between the general psychobabble pop culture understanding of ego and some of the deeper
sentences.zh: 精神分析研究，以及对它是什么、它有什么目的、它为什么存在的定性，因为正如我所说，这里有很大的区别。

sentences.en: psychoanalytic research and characterization of what this is, what purpose it serves, why it exists, because like I said, there is a big difference here.
sentences.zh: 心理学家多年来一直在定义和重新定义“自我”。

sentences.en: Psychologists have been defining and redefining the ego for many, many years.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实需要从弗洛伊德开始，才能对它旨在解释的内容有一个很好的鸟瞰视角。

sentences.en: But we really need to start at Freud to get a good bird's eye view of what it was intended to explain.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德是第一位真正将“自我”概念引入该领域的心理学家。

sentences.en: So Freud was the first psychologist to really introduce the idea of ego into this field.
sentences.zh: 我真的无法夸大他当时关于这个主题的文章所引发的波澜，直到今天依然如此。

sentences.en: And I really cannot overstate the waves that his essay on this created at the time and still to this day.
sentences.zh: 我会说他最初关于这个主题的论文可能是心理学领域有史以来最具影响力或最著名的论文之一。

sentences.en: I would say his initial paper on this is possibly one of the most influential or famous papers ever written in the field of psychology.
sentences.zh: 由于他的想法是如此新颖，它为几代人创造了全新的研究领域。

sentences.en: It has created entirely new fields of research and studies for generations because of how novel his ideas really were.
sentences.zh: 所以对弗洛伊德来说，我们的“自我”确实与我们的自我意识相连。

sentences.en: So for Freud, our ego is really attached to our sense of self.
sentences.zh: 在拉丁语中，“ego”字面意思就是“我”或“自我”。

sentences.en: And in Latin, ego literally means I or me or self.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的潜意识也被称为“自我”。

sentences.en: So our unconscious mind also referred to as the self.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，它与“自我”是一样的。

sentences.en: So in some ways, the same as ego.
sentences.zh: 它受三件事控制，三个独特的、都在争夺控制权的影响因素。

sentences.en: It's controlled by three things, three unique influences who are all striving for control.
sentences.zh: 首先是“自我”（ego）。

sentences.en: Firstly, the ego.
sentences.zh: 然后是“本我”（id）。

sentences.en: And then we have the id.
sentences.zh: 最后是“超我”（super ego）。

sentences.en: And finally, the super ego.
sentences.zh: 后两者在我们的讨论中被忽略了，因为它们被视为这里主角的配角。

sentences.en: So the last two are kind of left out of our conversations on this because they're seen as kind of secondary characters to the main player here.
sentences.zh: 我们的“本我”是我们思想中非常原始、本能、狂野的部分，它控制着攻击性、性冲动等事物。

sentences.en: So our id is this very primitive, instinctual, wild part of our mind that is in control of things like aggression, like our sexual urges.
sentences.zh: 它受弗洛伊德所说的“快乐原则”驱动。

sentences.en: It's driven by what Freud called the pleasure principle.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们思想中许多人试图压抑的部分。

sentences.en: So that's part of our mind which many of us try to suppress.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是我们思想中真正渴望深层、情感、原始释放的部分，是对我们所有欲望、所有需求

sentences.en: The kind, you know, the part of our mind which is really striving for deep, emotional, primitive release, the instant gratification of all of our desires, all of our wants
sentences.zh: 和需要的即时满足，无论付出什么代价。

sentences.en: and our needs really at whatever coSt.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果我们任由这一面自由发展，那将是极具社会破坏性和混乱的。

sentences.en: Now, if we let that side of us run freely, it would be incredibly socially disruptive and chaotic.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是“超我”发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: So this is where our super ego comes in.
sentences.zh: 这是我们潜意识的一部分，它充当了那种非常狂野、难以驾驭、

sentences.en: And this is the subconscious part of our mind that kind of acts as a counterbalance to that really wild, unruly,
sentences.zh: 本能部分的制衡力量。

sentences.en: instinctual part of us.
sentences.zh: 如果说在这种情况下“本我”是魔鬼，那么“超我”就是天使，它是我们所有深层道德本能、我们向善欲望的持有者。

sentences.en: So if the id in this situation is kind of the devil, the super ego is really the angel, kind of the holder of all of our deep moral instincts, our desire to be good.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，“超我”包含了所有那些代代相传的内化道德标准和理想，来自我们的家庭、

sentences.en: And importantly, the super ego is what contains all of those internalized moral standards and ideals that have been passed from generation to generation from our families,
sentences.zh: 我们的父母、我们的社会。

sentences.en: from our parents, from our society.
sentences.zh: 它确实是我们的是非观，在某种程度上试图使我们文明化。

sentences.en: It's really our sense of right and wrong that tries to in some ways civilize us.
sentences.zh: 所以“本我”和“超我”在争夺我们思想的控制权。

sentences.en: So the id and the super ego are kind of in this deep battle for control of our mind.
sentences.zh: 而我们的“自我”在这里扮演着家长的角色。

sentences.en: and our ego is the parent here.
sentences.zh: 我们的“自我”是最终的决策者。

sentences.en: Our ego is the final decider.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的“自我”需要做的是平衡这两者，并试图就我们如何行动做出某种决定。

sentences.en: So what our ego needs to do is balance both of these things and try and come to some kind of decision about how we act.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在我们确实认为“自我”与傲慢或一种过度膨胀、不自然的自我价值感是同义词。

sentences.en: And I think these days we really think of the ego as synonymous with things like arrogance or a really expanded unnatural sense of self-worth.
sentences.zh: 但对弗洛伊德来说，“自我”是我们控制现实的部分，是我们吸收来自“本我”的所有冲动和欲望，以及来自“超我”的所有善意，

sentences.en: But for Freud, our ego was the part of us in control of reality, the part of us which takes in all of the urges and the impulses from the id and then all of the good intentions
sentences.zh: 并就我们想如何向世界展示自己、我们真正想采取什么行动做出明智决定的部分。

sentences.en: of the super ego and makes an informed decision about how we want to represent ourselves to the world, what actions we actually want to take.
sentences.zh: 所以我在这里举一个简短的例子来真正说明这一点。

sentences.en: So I'm going to give a quick example here to kind of really nail in this point.
sentences.zh: 假设你和某人约会了几个月，他们做了一些让你非常恼火的事情。

sentences.en: Say you've been dating someone for a few months and they do something that really annoys you.
sentences.zh: 也许他们放了你鸽子，也许他们忘了回你短信，或者他们喝得太醉，做了什么蠢事。

sentences.en: Maybe they stand you up, maybe they forget to text you back or they get too drunk or do something stupid.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，我们必然会感受到的愤怒和恼火将来自“本我”，你这一部分可能真的想发泄、想暴怒、想对他们

sentences.en: In that moment, the anger and the annoyance that we're bound to feel is going to come from the id and this part of you might really want to lash out to be furious, to give them
sentences.zh: 冷暴力，想做那些可能让你当下感觉好一点，但我们知道从长远来看可能会破坏

sentences.en: the silent treatment, to do the things that might make you feel in the moment a lot better but that we know in the long run are probably actually going to sabotage
sentences.zh: 那段关系的事情。

sentences.en: that relationship.
sentences.zh: 所以另一方面，我们有“超我”，这是我们内心推动我们去宽恕、以一种非常情感纯粹的方式行事的部分，有时

sentences.en: So on the other side, we have our super ego and this is the part of us that is pushing us to forgive, to act in a way that is very emotionally pure and also at times
sentences.zh: 也许有点太被动了，而“自我”在这里的角色是平衡这两种观点，并以一种相当理性的、

sentences.en: perhaps a little bit too passive and the ego's role here is to balance both of those perspectives and act in a quite rational,
sentences.zh: 自我实现的方式行事。

sentences.en: self-fulfilling way.
sentences.zh: 所以对弗洛伊德来说，拥有一个强大、受控的“自我”意味着拥有强烈的自我意识。
